title.narrative: Peaceful elections and transtion;Conversation of faiths Project

description.narrative:
The Catholic Archdiocese of Mombasa in collaboration with other stakeholders proposes to mobilise and prepare a team of religious leaders to promote dialogue, understanding and cooperation in tackling the growing religious suspicion and a new wave of religious fundamentalism in the coastal region. The project is twofold, one is sensitization of faith leaders on how to address the challenge of growing religious suspicion and a new wave of religious fundamentalism, and manage the engagement with political leaders from this region on addressing the historical injustices and two, setting up of an interfaith team to monitor, gather information and distil it for advocacy. The project aims to build safe and supportive networks for inter-faith dialogue and conversation of faiths. The project targets religious leaders in the Archdiocese of Mombasa. The project will include: o Inter-faith conferences, o Dialogue circles among faith communities, o Joint inter-faith services, o Emergency preparedness in view of upcoming elections Archdiocese of Mombasa through its Justice and Peace Com will promote tolerance by working with religious leaders through the Coast Interfaith Council of Clerics (CICC), District Peace Committees (DPCs) and other influential community leaders. CJPC will build the capacity of these groups in early warning and early response, peace building and conflict management (PBCM) and alternative dispute resolution (ADR) skills in five (5) flash point areas prone to violence and negative ethnicity within Kilifi, Kwale and Mombasa counties. The enhanced capacity will enable the selected religious leaders, DPCs and community opinion leaders serve as peace ambassadors and spearhead dialogue forums and community outreach activities between different communities within the identified flash point areas. With regard to objective two, Caritas Mombasa will train teams of respected and committed community members on incident debriefing as well as psycho-social support. It is expected that we shall have able persons to provide community-friendly counselling services and attend focus group discussions (FGDs) in order to identify cases that need psycho-social support and where possible support them or refer them using the referral systems set.
Tentative proposed areas include Likoni, Majengo, Kisauni (Mombasa County), Ukunda (Kwale) Kipini (Tana River) and Kaloleni (Kilifi). The exact localities will be mapped out after final consultations with Ecumenical leaders and District Peace committee members. The estimated number of program beneficiaries is about 5,000 people.
